title: Create hostile review queue MCP tool and normalized results
description: Create a hostile review queue as an MCP tool that lets an agent request adversarial review of code, documentation, implementation plans, requirements, or other project artifacts.
Allow the request to link MCP artifacts as reviewer context, including TODOs, requirements, session logs, triage reports, files, commits, plans, and generated documents where supported.
Persist review results in a fully normalized schema so failure modes can be analyzed by workspace, requesting agent, reviewer agent/model, model name, effort level, review target type, and time.
Capture the reviewer opinion of request quality, including adequacy of artifact disclosure, review scope definition, and clarity/actionability of the request.
technicalDetails: Define request, queue item, artifact link, review execution, reviewer identity, model identity, effort level, finding, recommendation, verdict, and request-quality assessment entities.
The MCP tool must accept bounded review requests with target type, requested review mode, scope statement, artifact links, requester identity, workspace identity, and optional acceptance criteria.
Artifact links must resolve through supported MCP artifact APIs rather than raw file/database access, with diagnostics for missing, unauthorized, stale, or ambiguous artifacts.
Normalized results must distinguish actual defects, risks, missing tests, unclear requirements, insufficient disclosure, out-of-scope concerns, and reviewer uncertainty.
Track model and effort level explicitly for reviewer runs, including provider/model string, effective effort level, agent identity, plugin/source surface, prompt template/version, and run metadata.

Request-quality scoring must include artifact disclosure adequacy, scope clarity, review objective clarity, reviewer confidence, and whether the request contained enough context for a defensible review.
Provide query/reporting surfaces for failure modes by workspace, model including effort, agent, artifact type, and review category.
Default behavior is queue-and-record; any automated code/document mutation from review output requires a separate explicit workflow.

implementationTasks.task: Register BDPv4 FR/TR/TEST requirements and acceptance criteria for hostile review queue, artifact linking, normalized results, and analytics dimensions.
Inspect existing review, triage, TODO, requirements, session-log, model metadata, MCP tool, REPL, and plugin conventions before designing schemas.
Design normalized storage for review requests, artifact links, reviewer runs, findings, verdicts, request-quality assessments, model metadata, and failure-mode taxonomy.
Implement the MCP tool for submitting hostile review requests with workspace scoping, requester identity, artifact link validation, queue status, and bounded payload limits.
Implement artifact ingestion/resolution for MCP TODO, FR/TR/TEST requirements, session logs, triage reports, plans, files, commits, docs, and generated artifacts using supported APIs.
Implement reviewer execution/result capture pipeline that records model, effort level, agent identity, prompt/template version, token/runtime metadata where available, and deterministic run IDs.
Implement normalized result writing for findings, risks, missing context, scope issues, recommendations, verdicts, confidence, and request-quality dimensions.
Add query/reporting APIs for failure modes by workspace, model, effort level, requesting agent, reviewer agent, target type, artifact type, severity, and category.
Add REPL/Director/plugin skill surfaces for submitting review requests, checking queue status, and reading normalized review results.
Add tests for schema normalization, artifact link validation, request-quality scoring, model/effort attribution, workspace isolation, malformed requests, missing artifacts, and analytics queries.
Update documentation, requirements mappings, generated wiki exports, and agent guidance after tests are green.
